cards.text: Jesus is wrapping up a long teaching for His disciples, and He saves this one for last. The Son of Man, the name Jesus uses for Himself, comes in His glory with ALL the angels. Then He sits on His glorious throne.

cards.question: When the Son of Man is seated on His glorious throne, who is gathered before Him?

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats." Now THAT is sorting, friend. Not like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, who swore every single one of them belonged in the "still works" pile.

cards.question: The Son of Man will place the sheep on His ___ and the goats on His ___.

cards.text: Now Jesus calls Him the King, and the King speaks to the ones on His right. His first word? "Come." Not "Who let you in?" Not "Your name's not on the list." COME.

cards.question: The King tells the ones on His right, who are blessed by His Father, to inherit something. What is it?
The King says this kingdom was put together for them at the last minute.

cards.text: Then the King tells them why: when He was hungry, they gave Him something to eat, and when He was thirsty, they gave Him something to drink.

cards.question: The King keeps going. He says He was a ___ and they took Him in.
The King also says that when He was sick they looked after Him, and when He was in prison they visited Him.

cards.text: The righteous answer with a question: "Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You something to drink?" I bet it feels like getting a thank-you card for a favor you don't even remember doing.

cards.question: The righteous go down the King's list: hungry, thirsty, a stranger, naked, sick, in prison. What do they keep asking Him?

answers.text: When they ever saw Him that way
Why He never told them sooner
How He made it through all that

cards.question: The King answers the righteous, "Truly I tell you." What does He say about whatever they did for one of the least of these brothers of His?

cards.text: Then the King turns to the ones on His left, and this part is heavy, friend. Instead of "Come," He says, "Depart from Me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire".

cards.question: The King says the eternal fire was prepared for someone. Who is it?

cards.text: Then the King gives the reason, and it's that list again. When He was hungry, they gave Him nothing to eat, and when He was thirsty, they gave Him nothing to drink.

cards.question: The King says the ones on His left did cruel things to Him when He was a stranger, naked, sick and in prison.
Just like the righteous, the ones on the King's left ask Him when they ever saw Him in need.
The King answers the ones on His left, "Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for ___."

cards.text: And this is where Jesus lands it. The ones on the left go away into eternal punishment.

cards.question: The ones on the left go away into eternal punishment. Where does Jesus say the righteous go?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "Who let you in?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "Truly I tell you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.
A blank is a word that matters to the meaning, never a word like "or," "and" or "he."

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card states two facts from outside the passage with no reference: that Jesus is teaching His disciples (Matthew 24:3) and that Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself. The card cites only Matthew 25:31.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card, but it has three sentences: the quote from Jesus, "Now THAT is sorting, friend," and the battery joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "side" is a near-match. Both right and left are sides of the throne, so a baker could argue that "side" fits either blank.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card runs to about five sentences: "Now Jesus calls Him the King...", "His first word?", "Come.", "Not 'Who let you in?'", "Not 'Your name's not on the list.'" and "COME."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card quotes the righteous asking "Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You...?" The very next choice card (stop 1, card 12) asks what the righteous keep asking, and its right answer is "When they ever saw Him that way." The story card gives that answer away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card cites Matthew 25:42-43, but it tells only the content of 25:42 (hungry and thirsty). The items from 25:43 are not told on this card. They are asked on the next card.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The statement covers only stranger, naked, sick and in prison, which are all in Matthew 25:43. The card cites Matthew 25:42-43. It should cite Matthew 25:43.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.
